title: Progressive Exposure Choreography — Playbook (WIP)
body:
Purpose:
This doc is a practical working playbook for choreographing progressive exposure (canary / A/B / staged rollouts) across multiple teams when introducing inference changes: model variants, routing policies, batching, quantization profiles, or cost-reduction features that could affect latency/quality/cost. The focus is on clear handoffs, fast observability-to-action loops, and minimizing blast radius while preserving the ability to iterate rapidly.

Audience and scope:
- Primary: Product, Eng (serving runtime, infra, SRE), Data/Applied ML, Developer Experience, Customer Success.
- Scope: rollout steps from initial hypothesis through full ramp. Covers traffic partitioning, cohort sequencing, signal thresholds, communications, and post-rollout cleanup. Intentionally operational and example-driven rather than theoretical.

High-level principles (short):
1) Small, measurable exposures — prefer more steps with smaller increments.
2) Signal-driven decisions — define primary/secondary metrics and strict gating thresholds before traffic flows.
3) Clear ownership — each signal has an owner who can act (pause/rollback) without coordination latency.
4) Safe defaults — any new routing should default to the stable backend unless explicit opt-in.
5) Observability-first — instrumented canaries are non-negotiable (latency by token/request, cost, quality).

Quick glossary (team shorthand):
- Exposure bucket: a named traffic cohort (e.g., bucket-alpha-1) with a fixed allocation and guardrails.
- Traffic shepherd: the person/team actively monitoring and controlling exposure adjustments during the rollout window.
- Safety fence: automated check (SLO or alert) that pauses traffic for a bucket when a threshold is breached.

Before you start (preflight checklist):
- Hypothesis canvas: one-sentence hypothesis + expected metric deltas (e.g., "quantize-int8 reduces token-cost 25% with <=1% quality regression").
- Baseline snapshot: capture current P50/P95 latency, tokens-per-request, cost-per-1k-tokens, end-to-end error rate, and a small quality eval set results. Timestamp and store artifact.
- Define success gates and rollback gates (numerical thresholds). Document in the rollout ticket.
- Define cohorts and sequence (e.g., internal staff -> superusers -> 1% random -> 5% random -> 25% -> 100%). Map cohorts to exposure buckets.
- Automated safety fences implemented in the console/traffic router (threshold config + throttling/pause action).
- Alert routing and paging set up for the running window. Pager owners must be identified.

Cohort design and sequencing considerations:
- Start with non-production or internal opt-ins (staff, integrations team) for sanity.
- Use alpha cohorts tied to specific user attributes when possible (platform team, low-risk customers).
- For latency/cost focused changes, prefer request-sliced exposures (e.g., sample 1% of requests) instead of user-sliced (1% of users) to reduce exposure time for bursty users. For quality-sensitive features, prefer user-sliced cohorts.
- Consider sticky routing semantics for user experience: decide whether users in an exposure should remain in the same bucket for session-length or be re-sampled. Document the choice.

Traffic shaping patterns (practical knobs):
- Ramp schedule (example): 0.1% -> 0.5% -> 1% -> 2% -> 5% -> 10% -> 25% -> 100% with 1–24h observation windows depending on traffic volume.
- Timebox and step size: smaller steps with longer observation windows for quality-sensitive changes; faster ramps for purely cost-optimizations when quality already validated.
- Backfill vs forward-only: for experiments that change user-visible text, avoid backfilling historical sessions. For infrastructure changes (e.g., batching), forward-only is acceptable.

Observability matrix (define owners):
- Primary signal: user-facing quality metric (e.g., eval pass rate, human-labeled quality delta) — owner: applied-ml.
- Secondary signals: end-to-end latency P50/P95 (owner: serving-runtime), token cost / request (owner: finance/ops), error rate (owner: SRE), downstream service saturation (owner: infra).
- Tertiary signals: UX metrics (engagement click-through, time-to-first-prompt), CS tickets volume.

Safety fences and automated closures:
- Safety fences should be codified and testable. Example thresholds:
  - latency_p95 > baseline_p95 * 1.4 for 5m -> auto-pause bucket
  - error_rate > 3x baseline or >0.5% absolute for 5m -> auto-pause
  - quality_eval_drop >= 2% absolute -> immediate halt and notify applied-ml + PM
- Automated pause actions should trigger: (a) rollback to stable variant OR (b) route remaining traffic to a compatible fallback model. Both actions need documented runbook steps.

Roles & responsibilities (choreography matrix):
- Product (PM): defines hypothesis, success criteria, customer comms.
- Applied ML: quality evals, labeling triage, twilight testing.
- Serving runtime: implements routing config, safety fences, deploys variant.
- SRE/Infra: monitors infra signals, escalates, performs capacity adjustments if needed.
- DevEx/SDK: updates client-side flags or docs for any opt-ins.
- Customer Success: pre-alert for impacted customers and run cohort-specific outreach if issues surface.
- Incident commander on-call: final rollback decision if automated systems fail.

Communication cadence during ramp:
- Pre-rollout: async announcement in #prod-rollouts with ticket link, burn-in window, and primary contacts.
- Hourly check-ins during first 4 steps (chat updates + short status line in playbook).
- Escalation calls if any safety fence trips.
- Post-ramp summary within 24h to stakeholders with key metrics and any follow-ups.

Experiment analysis and metrics to capture per step:
- N (requests) and unique users in bucket
- P50/P95 latency by bucket
- Token consumption per request and cost-per-1k-tokens
- Quality eval samples and automated metric deltas (BLEU/ROUGE/embedding-sim if applicable)
- Error types and stack traces (top 5)
- Downstream service CPU/GPU utilization and queue length
- CS tickets and customer-visible incidents

Decision gates and example rules:
- Continue -> if primary signal within +/- X% of baseline and no safety fence violations for observation window.
- Pause -> if safety fence triggered. Pause is reversible after triage and fix, followed by a reduced re-ramp.
- Rollback -> if catastrophic regression (predefined: quality_drop > Y% or outage), immediately route traffic to stable variant and open an incident.

Post-rollout and learning loop:
- Postmortem template: include hypothesis, metric deltas, timeline, decisions, root cause, follow-ups, owners, and whether to codify changes in the runbook.
- If rollout succeeded: schedule follow-up to deprecate old variant and migrate any long-lived experiment flags.
- If failed: define remediation plan and a conservative reintroduce schedule.

Operational checklists (copyable):
- 30m before traffic: verify observability dashboards, alerting, and auto-pause configured; confirm owners and on-call.
- 5m before first sample: publish rollout note in channel and set status message.
- Every step: record bucket size, time started, metrics snapshot, and decision rationale.

Examples / quick scenarios:
1) Routing policy change to prefer quantized model for low-latency endpoints: start with 0.1% request-slice for 2h; monitor p95, cost, quality test set. If p95 improves and quality delta <0.5%, continue.
2) A/B content change that affects engagement: prefer user-sliced cohorts with sticky assignment for 24h; measure CTR and manual label set for quality.

Open questions and followups (to resolve pre-rollout):
- Who has the automated button to unpause? (Ops vs Product?) Recommend SRE/serving runtime own the auto-pause + automatic fallback, with PM/APPLIED-ML authorization for re-ramp.
- Standardize step durations by experiment category (security, quality-sensitive, cost-only).
- Improve tooling for faster quality eval sampling and triage integration with labeling queue.

Appendix: Suggested template to create rollout ticket (copy into issue body):
1) Hypothesis, owners, success/rollback gates (numeric)
2) Baseline snapshot artifacts and links
3) Cohort plan and ramp schedule
4) Observability links and dashboard names
5) Safety fence config (thresholds + actions)
6) Communication plan and escalation path
7) Postmortem and cleanup checklist

Notes / working ideas (brainstorm):
- "Temporal smoothing" for small buckets: hold new buckets open for a minimal 15m window before evaluating to reduce noise from short bursts.
- Combine a fast request-slice for initial sanitation with a user-slice for sustained evaluation to get both early signal and realistic UX.
- Auto-annotate any safety fence pause with top 3 signals that triggered (latency spike, error type, quality eval) to speed triage.

History and versioning:
- 2025-11-03 initial draft by Maya Patel
- 2025-12-12 added safety fence patterns (Ethan Zhao)
- 2026-03-05 expanded roles/choreography matrix (Lena Rodríguez)

Action items next:
- Align with SRE to standardize automated pause actions (owner: Connor Hayes, due 2026-03-19).
- Prototype a dashboard template for rollout windows (owner: DevEx, Priya Singh, due 2026-03-25).

End of playbook (WIP): keep evolving based on postmortems and live rollouts.
